_comment: The missions (SPEC.md §12 M27, ROADMAP.md Phase 2): the game is an engine plus a mission. Each entry is printed on the contents page, in this order. `status` is `playable` or `coming`; a coming mission is printed but stamped NEXT YEAR'S ANNUAL and cannot be chosen, so it needs only `id`, `title`, `place`, `page` and `blurb`. A playable one names its `map` and `roster` files, and a `rules` and `enemies` patch deep-merged over data/rules.json and data/enemies.json before the difficulty's (the same merge difficulty.json uses; a key must already exist, except a new objective kind under `objectives` or a new enemy type under `types`). `win` is one of the fixed win conditions in src/missions.js, never a code branch for one mission. `briefing` opens the orders; `tagline` runs along the foot of the title card; `words` are the mission's own phrases the rules' text needs; `titleCard` is its painted title card (ART-ASSETS.md §7); `endSounds` are the sound.js cues for the back page. `?mission=<id>` in the address picks one, and `default` is the one when none is asked for.

missions.title: The Rail Bridge
missions.blurb: Six men drop by night to blow the bridge that carries the line to the coast, and must be out before dawn.
missions.tagline: SIX MEN · ONE BRIDGE · DAWN AT TWENTY
missions.briefing: Tonight six men are to drop behind enemy lines.

missions.title: The Airfield
missions.blurb: Aircraft in their pens on an Axis landing ground, one charge each. Every one more is greed against the dawn.

missions.title: The Aqueduct
missions.blurb: A great aqueduct in the mountains that wants every charge you carry, and a boat on the coast that will not wait.
